issues.legal_issue: A pre-constitutional sovereign order suspending an immediate right to possession is not undone merely by the Constitution coming into force.
material_facts: A sovereign order made before the Constitution directed that the property remain under government supervision pending enquiry and kept any claimant’s right to immediate possession in abeyance until the right was established in the civil courts.
issues.conclusion: The Constitution did not restore any right to immediate possession that had been held in abeyance by the pre-constitutional order.
issues.legal_principle: The Constitution guarantees the rights a person held when it came into force; it does not add to or restore rights already removed or suspended. Under Article 13(1), an inconsistent pre-constitutional law is not obliterated for past transactions and accrued rights or liabilities. The Court applied Syed Qasim Razi v. State of Hyderabad and distinguished Ameerunnissa Begum v. Mahboob Begum, which concerned a Firman issued after the Constitution.

predicates.preconstitutional_sovereign_order: A sovereign issued the order before the Constitution came into force.
predicates.order_suspended_immediate_possession: The order kept claimants from immediate possession pending an enquiry or a court determination.

issues.definition: When a pre-constitutional sovereign order kept immediate possession suspended, the rights it affected were not automatically restored merely because the Constitution came into force.

issues.legal_issue: Mandamus cannot compel delivery of property when the applicant has no present right to possession established by a court.
material_facts: The applicant sought mandamus compelling the government department to hand over management and possession of the property.
The pre-constitutional order required a claimant to establish a right to possession in the civil courts before seeking restoration.
No civil court decision declared the applicant’s right to possession.
issues.conclusion: The applicant had no present right to possession, so mandamus could not issue.
issues.legal_principle: Mandamus cannot issue where the applicant has no present right to demand the act sought. Under the sovereign order, a claimant’s right to possession remained in abeyance until established in the civil courts; the Court did not decide whether mandamus would be an appropriate remedy if such a right were later established.

predicates.mandamus_application: A person applies for mandamus seeking an order that a public authority deliver property or its management.
predicates.possession_right_conditioned_on_court_es: An order governing the property makes restoration of possession dependent on the claimant establishing a right in court.
predicates.no_court_declaration_of_applicant_right: No court has declared that the applicant is entitled to possession.

issues.definition: If a person seeks mandamus to obtain property whose possession is subject to a court-established right, and no court has declared the applicant’s entitlement, mandamus is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: The dismissal of a rival claimant’s civil suit does not itself establish the applicant’s right to possession.
material_facts: A rival claimant brought a civil suit concerning the property, and the suit was dismissed.
The civil court judgment did not declare that the applicant was entitled to possession; it found that the claimed office was not proved for any party.
issues.conclusion: The rival claimant’s failure in the civil litigation did not establish the applicant’s right to possession under the order requiring that right to be established in court.
issues.legal_principle: Where an order makes restoration dependent on establishing one’s own right in a civil court, the failure of a rival’s claim is not a judicial determination that the applicant has that right. The civil judgment must declare the applicant’s entitlement; the relative strength of the parties’ evidence or the rival’s unsuccessful suit does not substitute for that determination.

predicates.prior_civil_suit: A civil suit was brought concerning rights to the property by a rival claimant.
predicates.rival_claim_dismissed: The rival claimant’s civil suit was dismissed.
predicates.no_court_declaration_of_applicant_right: The civil court did not declare that the applicant was entitled to possession.

issues.definition: When a rival’s civil suit is dismissed without a declaration of the applicant’s entitlement, that dismissal does not establish the applicant’s right to possession.
